- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward to reflect bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is above recent low, adjust downward to reflect bearish pressure.  
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts after sharp price spikes; reduce overshoot by 10–15% in the immediate next period.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.6), favor mean reversion toward recent 7–14 day average rather than trend continuation.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from forecast in first 5 days, apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 5–10% for days 6–10 to account for delayed reaction.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal patterns (e.g., 2+ consecutive positive then negative), apply a “sentiment decay” rule: reduce forecast magnitude by 5–10% for each subsequent day after sentiment turns negative.
